attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, in his updated list of AI-bubble warning signs.

semantics.note: Unhedged 'will' conditional; the antecedent is kept. 'Things will look bad' is slightly narrowed to NVIDIA's earnings, but that is the natural reading given 'come earnings season'. No deadline was stated.

contract.note: Reading the antecedent as material payment failures, not longer agreed terms, and the consequence as a material adverse earnings effect is an ordinary financial reading. It is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: NVIDIA 10-Q, available 2026-08-27. It shows longer agreed payment terms for investment-grade customers and concentrated receivables, but no customer failing to pay when due. So it does not establish the antecedent.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet does not show NVIDIA customers materially failing to pay by the evaluation date: the 10-Q shows only extended agreed terms. With the antecedent unknown, the claim cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post that the beginnings of debt-raising trouble had already been seen at Lancaster.

semantics.note: The checkable part is the historical claim that Lancaster had financing trouble before 2026-03-31. The 'warning sign' framing is interpretive and is rightly left unscored.

contract.note: It fairly separates the project's financing partners from CoreWeave as tenant, does not require default, and says later bridge funding would not refute earlier trouble. Whether disputed reporting counts as corroborated is what decides the result.

evidence.note: Bisnow, 2026-02-20, passes on Business Insider's anonymously sourced report that lenders passed on the Lancaster debt, and carries Blue Owl's direct on-record denial. One disputed, uncorroborated report does not establish the difficulty or refute it.

reviews.rationale: The only readable evidence is secondhand coverage of one anonymously sourced report, set against a direct denial from Blue Owl, the party arranging the financing. The original report and any financing records were not checked. The packet neither confirms nor rules out pre-publication financing trouble at Lancaster.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, in his list of warning signs.

semantics.note: The draft calls this a conditional_forecast, yet the contract scores it as an observation. 'Loosest lender in the AI bubble' is a hyperbolic superlative with no comparison group, and 'a bad sign' names no measurable consequence. Neither part is a scoreable forecast.

contract.note: It turns a rhetorical jab into a strict ranking of underwriting across all AI lenders, and picks Q4 2025 itself because the speaker gave no period. This is not the ordinary reading; an informed reader takes 'loosest' as hyperbole.

evidence.note: Meta's own 2025-10-21 disclosure on the Hyperion joint venture: short initial leases offset by a residual value guarantee. It covers one deal, largely an equity stake by Blue Owl funds, so it cannot rank lenders.

reviews.rationale: The superlative names no lender group and no standard, and the conditional 'bad sign' has no testable outcome. The claim is too vague and rhetorical to score, and the contract's own choices about lender universe, period and weighting would decide any result. Not adjudicable.
